answer: Staggered relay timing gates new agents by requiring each identity’s first messages to pass a prism check that compares arrival gaps across independent relays. An identity must clear a randomized three-epoch warmup, sending one minimum-fee jade probe per epoch; matching timing vectors collapse into one cluster. A beacon at epoch end admits only clusters whose traffic shape stays irregular enough, so bulk parallel registrations fail. Each rejected sybil loses three probe fees and a full warmup delay, then must restart with a fresh timing vector.
